transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Daniel Reed (Redwood AE), Nina Kapoor (Redwood SE), Monica Hale (Lyra - Head of Search), Arman Bhatt (Lyra ML Eng), Priya Singh (Lyra Product), Sam (Lyra Legal - joined 00:22)

Auto-generated Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking. Walkthrough of Redwood Console routing, embedding endpoints, and reranker endpoint integration patterns. Discussed security (SOC2, KMS), pilot scope, and next steps for a 2-week hosted pilot.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint (batch vs streaming)
- Reranker API usage patterns and scoring thresholds
- Console eval/Optimize hints (batching, caching, quant profiles)
- Security & data residency (SOC2, SSO, KMS, retention)
- Pilot plan and success metrics

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Daniel from Redwood, AE on the account. We have Nina our solutions engineer, we'll do a quick 40 minute walkthrough and leave time for questions.
[00:17] Monica: Hey thanks. We, we are really eager, last week we talked about doing better search relevance for our knowledge base — apologies if we sound a bit scattered, timezone stuff.
[00:31] Daniel: No worries. Quick agenda, 1) show embeddings API and how to index, 2) demo rerank endpoint with live examples, 3) Console + Optimize tips for cost/latency, 4) security + pilot. Sound good?
[00:42] Monica: Yep.
[00:45] Nina: I'll share my screen in a second, but quick note up front — when I say "reranker" I'm referencing our hosted rerank endpoint which takes a query and preselected candidates and returns a score and optional explanation token spans. It's small latency overhead compared to full generation, but gives big lift for top-k ordering.
[01:05] Arman: Can you remind us what's the difference between the embeddings call and the rerank? We currently use an off-the-shelf vector DB.
[01:12] Nina: Sure. Embeddings endpoint is for encoding docs/queries into vectors — you push those into whatever vector DB you prefer. Rerank accepts the query plus a list of candidate doc ids or payloads and runs a lightweight relevance model on them using context + cached kv where applicable. So we often do a hybrid: vector retrieval first, then rerank top 50.
[01:34] Priya: Top 50 seems high, what's the latency impact?
[01:38] Nina: It depends on model and batch. For hosted we default to a quantized, low-latency rerank model; expect 40–120ms for 16 candidates, 200–400ms for 50 depending on load and whether you enable batching. We can show exact numbers in the console tracing.
[01:57] Monica: That's within range. Cost concerns though — reranking 50 per query could be expensive at scale.
[02:03] Daniel: Right — Redwood Optimize gives suggestions: dynamic top-k based on query complexity, caching repeated queries, and prefix/KV caching for doc context. Our Console will surface token-level cost; Nina can demo the tradeoff.
[02:18] Nina: Ok I'm sharing screen now... sorry if the resolution is noisy.
[02:30] [screen share noise]
[02:35] Nina: Here's the Console, top-left is model catalog. For Lyra I'd recommend starting with the 'rwrk-small-v1' reranker — low memory, tuned for semantic rerank. For embeddings, choose the 'emb-mid-128' for mid-sized vectors.
[02:56] Arman: Do you support different vector sizes for different pipelines? like 128 vs 256?
[03:01] Nina: Yes, you can pin model versions per route. We recommend 128 for latency-first, 256 if you need finer granularity. Also the Console shows a per-route latency/cost preview based on your sample distribution.
[03:19] Monica: Where do we upload our docs for the demo?
[03:22] Nina: You can upload via the Console, or use the API. For the pilot it's easiest to upload a sample bundle to the temporary S3 location we'll create. We'll share that link in the notes.
[03:35] Daniel: Quick security note before deep dive — we are SOC 2 Type II, support SAML SSO and customer KMS via our Private offering. For hosted pilots we offer encryption at rest and in transit and optional short-term retention. Sam from legal if you have specifics maybe jump in.
[03:55] Sam: Quick q — what's retention default for hosted? And do you have audit logs we can ingest?
[04:01] Daniel: Default is 30 days for pilot data but configurable; audit logs are available via our Console export (JSON) or a syslog endpoint. We'll include the security whitepaper in the follow-up.
[04:16] Sam: Thanks.
[04:20] Nina: Back to the demo — I'll run a sample flow: ingest docs, embed, run vector search in customer DB, then call rerank endpoint with candidate payloads.
[04:30] [keyboard clack]
[04:36] Nina: Step 1: embeddings call. Example curl: POST /v1/embeddings with model=emb-mid-128, payload is text chunk. We return a 128-d vector. Note compression/quantization options: you can store float32 or 8-bit quantized vectors if your DB supports it.
[04:55] Arman: Does Redwood manage embeddings storage?
[04:58] Nina: No, we don't force a vector store. Customers use Pinecone, OpenSearch, Milvus, etc. Our Console integrates with connectors and shows vector density stats.
[05:10] Monica: Ok show rerank please.
[05:12] Nina: Rerank endpoint: POST /v1/rerank {query:..., candidates:[{id:, snippet:, metadata:}]}. You can pass up to 100 candidates; default scoring is 0-1. We return scores plus optional evidence spans if you enable 'explain=true'.
[05:34] [00:05:34] Monica: In our previous setup we did cross-encoder rerank in-house but it's flaky on long docs. Does your reranker pull full doc context?
[05:43] Nina: We support passing context snippets per candidate (best practice: pre-trim to 512 tokens per candidate). For very long docs you can pass chunked candidates and we consolidate scores. Also our KV cache helps if you do multi-turn sessions.
[05:58] Arman: If we keep candidate snippets in our DB, does the rerank call re-fetch content or do we need to include text in payload?
[06:06] Nina: Two patterns: include snippet text in the payload (simpler, slightly heavier network cost) or pass IDs and let our routing fetch via connector if enabled. For hosted demos we'll typically pass text inline.
[06:20] [crosstalk]
[06:22] Priya: Show example query?
[06:24] Nina: Sure. I'm going to run a live query against our demo corpus — excuse slight lag.
[06:33] [typing, spinner sound]
[06:38] Nina: Query: "how do I configure SAML in the admin console" — vector retrieval returns 40 candidates, I'm going to rerank top 12.
[06:47] [rerank API call executed]
[06:52] Nina: Results: Score diffs show the top results move from a generic SSO doc to the exact admin steps. The explain token spans highlight where the match occurred — you'll see the phrase "SAML metadata" and "identity provider" flagged.
[07:08] Monica: Those spans are super helpful for surfacing exact steps.
[07:11] Nina: Yup. On Console we also show latency breakdown: embedding call, vector lookup, rerank call.
[07:20] Daniel: On cost: embedding calls are charged per embedding unit; rerank is charged per candidate scored. For the pilot we can give a cost estimate based on your QPS and average top-k. We'll include a spreadsheet.
[07:34] Arman: For our telemetry we need token-level tracing to reconcile costs — do you emit traces?
[07:40] Nina: Yes — Console exposes token and call-level traces per request id; you can export to your observability stack.
[07:48] Monica: One worry: we need to keep PII out of logs. How do you do redaction?
[07:54] Daniel: We have an opt-in redaction pipeline and customer-managed retention with the Private option. For hosted pilots we can enable basic redaction and short retention. We'll follow up with the security doc.
[08:08] Nina: Now a few Optimize tips — if you have a predictable query distribution, you can set batching windows at the route level to improve throughput. Also prefix caching for common query starts reduces embedding calls for repeated queries.
[08:23] Arman: Can Optimize suggest batch sizes automatically?
[08:26] Nina: Yes, Optimize runs a short analysis on sample traces and recommends batch/quant profiles and whether a smaller reranker model would meet your SLA. We surfaced a recommendation during onboarding for another customer and they halved cost.
[08:39] Priya: Nice. Anything special about retries/fallbacks? If rerank fails we want to fallback to vector-only ordering.
[08:47] Nina: Our routing policy supports soft-fallback: if rerank exceeds latency threshold or errors, we can fall back to vector score ordering and log a gating metric. You configure that per-route on the Console.
[08:58] [09:00] Daniel: Ok I'm going to switch to an example integration snippet for developers...
[09:05] [screen scroll]
[09:09] Daniel: Here's a nodejs snippet: call embeddings -> store vector -> at query time vector search -> call rerank with top candidates -> use returned scores to re-order. There's also a batching helper lib we provide.
[09:24] Arman: What about rate limits? We may have spiky traffic on product launches.
[09:28] Daniel: Hosted quotas are per-account; we can provision burst capacity. For enterprise we recommend Dedicated. For the pilot we'll set a soft cap and can raise it if needed.
[09:40] Monica: If we do Dedicated later, will the API surface change?
[09:44] Daniel: No, same API - that's a key Redwood promise: unified inference across hosted, Dedicated, and Private. SDKs are identical, just different routing and SLOs.
[09:55] Arman: Any pitfalls with embeddings dimensionality when moving between models?
[09:59] Nina: Yes — embeddings are not always compatible across models. If you change from 128 to 256 the vectors are different; we recommend re-embedding the corpus or running a compatibility layer and reindex. Optimize can estimate re-index cost.
[10:13] Priya: Let's talk pilot scope — what would you recommend for a 2-week pilot?
[10:17] Daniel: 1) ingest a representative slice (10-20k docs or 10-20 query/doc pairs), 2) run sampling and collect relevance judgments on top-5, 3) try tuning rerank top-k and caching, 4) measure latency and cost. Nina will provide a checklist.
[10:33] Monica: We can definitely provide ~15 query/doc pairs to start.
[10:36] Arman: We'll also share our current vector DB snapshot for sanity checks.
[10:40] Daniel: Great. Sam anything legal needs?
[10:43] Sam: I'll review the pilot T&Cs — we prefer short term retention and audit scope, so please include audit log export mechanism.
[10:51] Daniel: Will do.
[10:53] [pause]
[11:00] Nina: One other advanced topic — model variants for rerank. For high precision we have rerank-large which gives slightly better ranking but higher latency. For production you can do a canary: route 10% to rerank-large, 90% to rerank-small and measure click-through or relevance lift.
[11:20] Monica: Do you have a built-in A/B test in Console?
[11:23] Nina: Yes, rollout controls let you split traffic, do canaries, and auto-fallback. Also metric hooks so you can feed custom success metrics.
[11:33] Priya: About SSO and SAML — can we provision team access via SCIM?
[11:37] Daniel: We support SCIM for user provisioning and SAML for SSO. For the hosted pilot we'll add the team manually; for enterprise we set up SCIM integration.
[11:47] Arman: Are there any known limitation on doc size or candidate size?
[11:51] Nina: Candidates should be trimmed to ~512 tokens for best rerank performance. Docs larger than that should be chunked at indexing time.
[11:59] Monica: Could you show Console's cost breakdown for the demo route?
[12:03] Nina: Sure. On the right I have a cost simulation panel — for our sample workload it estimates $0.004 per query at top-10 rerank and $0.012 at top-50. That's just a sim, final depends on your actual traffic.
[12:21] Monica: Can we get a CSV export of that?
[12:24] Nina: Yes we'll export the scenario and include in the follow-up.
[12:29] [12:29] Daniel: Quick pause — any other security questions?
[12:32] Sam: Do you do external pen tests?
[12:35] Daniel: Yes we do annual third-party pentests and the report is available under NDA. We'll share the SOC2 report too.
[12:45] Monica: Okay sounds good.
[12:47] Nina: Now I'm going to show a slightly messy real world example where rerank changed the top answer to the exact FAQ paragraph.
[12:55] [demo run]
[13:05] Nina: Notice the TF-IDF baseline had a topical match, but reranker prioritized the step-by-step guide. This is typical — rerank can bring down false positives.
[13:20] Arman: One more technical: how do you maintain KV cache consistency when content updates?
[13:26] Nina: The KV cache is per session, short-lived. For freshness we recommend invalidating cache on content update events; Console has hooks to help automate that.
[13:35] Daniel: We're at 35 minutes in — would you like to go deeper into any of the areas?
[13:41] Monica: Could we see the sample notebook? Not necessary to watch live, a link is fine.
[13:44] Daniel: We'll share the repo link.
[13:47] Priya: On metrics, could we define success as top-3 relevance increase by X%? We need measurable KPI.
[13:53] Daniel: Yep that's perfect. Typical pilot KPI is 10–15% uplift in top-3 click-through or NDCG. We'll help instrument evals.
[14:04] Arman: Perf testing — can we run a small benchmark from our region? Latency varies by region.
[14:09] Nina: Yes, we can run synthetic benchmarks from your region. For hosted we have region endpoints— we'll provision EU or us-west as needed.
[14:20] Sam: Any compliance for data residency?
[14:23] Daniel: Hosted supports region pinning in most cloud regions; for strict residency we offer Private deployment.
[14:31] Monica: Ok let's recap next steps.
[14:34] Daniel: Recap: Daniel will send pricing & pilot terms, Nina will send demo notebook and Console clip, Lyra will share sample queries/docs and shortlist pilot KPIs, Sam will review T&Cs. We'll plan kickoff next week.
[14:48] Monica: Great, sounds good.
[14:51] Priya: Quick note — can we get a quick price estimate for 100k monthly queries at top-10 rerank?
[14:58] Daniel: We'll include that in the pricing spreadsheet.
[15:02] Arman: Any final concerns?
[15:05] Monica: None from me.
[15:07] Daniel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[15:12] [meeting coversation trails off, some pleasantries]
